name: symbolic_math
title: Symbolic Math
summary: Exact symbolic mathematics using SymPy: differentiate, integrate (indefinite and definite), evaluate limits, solve equations, and simplify or factor expressions. All inputs and results are exchanged as strings and JSON-friendly values.

tools.name: evaluate_limit
tools.description: Evaluate the exact limit of an expression as a variable approaches a point, optionally from one side or both sides.

params.name: point
params.description: Value approached by the variable, such as '0', 'oo', '-oo', or 'pi/2'.

params.name: direction
params.description: Limit direction: '+' for right, '-' for left, or '+-' for two-sided. Defaults to '+'.

returns.name: result
returns.description: The evaluated limit as a string.

tools.implementation_notes: Import sympy. Convert expression, variable, and point with sympy.sympify. Call sympy.limit(expr, var, point, dir=direction or '+'). Convert the returned SymPy object to a string with str(result).

tools.name: simplify_or_factor_expression
tools.description: Simplify an expression heuristically or factor it into irreducible factors over the rationals.

params.name: deep
params.description: When operation is 'factor', whether to factor subexpressions. Defaults to false.

params.name: ratio
params.description: When operation is 'simplify', maximum allowed growth ratio of result complexity. Defaults to 1.7.

returns.name: result
returns.description: The simplified or factored expression as a string.

tools.implementation_notes: Import sympy. Convert expression with sympy.sympify. If operation is 'factor', call sympy.factor(expr, deep=deep). Otherwise call sympy.simplify(expr, ratio=ratio). Convert the returned SymPy object to a string with str(result).

side_effects: No persistent side effects in normal use.
sympy.sympify uses eval internally, so unsanitized or untrusted expression strings should not be passed.
uncertainties: Expression strings must use SymPy/Python syntax; implicit multiplication such as '2x' is not accepted by sympify.
Variable inference for solve is delegated to SymPy and may fail for some expressions.
solve output can vary by input form; this interface normalizes dict=True output to a list of variable-to-string mappings.
Integration may return unevaluated Integral, Piecewise, or conditional expressions.
Limits may return special values such as oo, -oo, zoo, or nan.
simplify uses heuristics and may leave an expression unchanged or make it longer; factor defaults to factorization over the rationals.
Bounds, points, and variables are converted with sympify, so symbolic bounds such as 'oo' and 'pi' are supported but invalid strings raise SympifyError.
